leh.html: Ancient monasteries, crystalline lakes, and mountain passes that steal your breath — literally.
A high-altitude cold desert in the northernmost reaches of India, Leh-Ladakh is a landscape unlike anywhere else on Earth. Barren mountains shimmer in impossible colours at dawn.
Buddhist monasteries cling to cliffsides. Pangong Lake shifts from blue to turquoise to green. For solo travellers who want to be truly alone with the universe — this is it.
Fly into Leh Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport (direct from Delhi, Mumbai, Srinagar). Road trips via Manali-Leh Highway or Srinagar-Leh Highway are legendary but require acclimatisation stops.
Steamed Tibetan dumplings — the ultimate Ladakhi comfort food.
Hearty noodle soup that warms your soul at 3500m altitude.
Salty, yak-butter tea — an acquired taste and a local tradition.
The most popular backpacker base in Ladakh with stunning views.
Centrally located budget hotel with warm hospitality.
"The silence of Pangong Lake at 5am is something I will carry forever. Ladakh does something to your soul."
"Hardest trip I've ever done, most beautiful thing I've ever seen. Acclimatise properly!"
Spend 2 days in Leh before going higher
Dress in layers — temperature swings wildly
UV protection essential at high altitude
Inform someone of your route always
manali.html: Rohtang Pass, apple orchards, paragliding — Manali is where mountains meet magic.
Nestled in the Kullu Valley, Manali is Himachal Pradesh's crown jewel. Ringed by peaks draped in snow and pine forests that seem to touch the sky, it's a year-round playground.
From skiing in Solang Valley to the sacred Hadimba Temple's cedar forest, from roaring Beas River to hidden Naggar Castle — Manali has more layers than its mountains.
Manali is best reached by overnight Volvo bus from Delhi (13-14 hrs). The nearest airport is Kullu-Manali Airport (Bhuntar), 50km away. Rohtang permit required for passes.
Himachali steamed bread stuffed with walnuts and poppy seeds — a mountain delicacy.
Fresh Himalayan trout from Beas River, lightly spiced and unforgettable.
Traditional Himachali feast served on leaf plates — rice, lentils, curd, and rajma.
Cosy hostel in Old Manali with mountain views and great community vibe.
Budget riverside resort with stunning Beas views.
"Paraglided over Solang Valley on my first solo trip. My heart was in my throat but my soul was flying."
"Old Manali cafes, snowfall at night, Hidimba temple at dawn. This place is pure poetry."

Carry basic first aid and medicines
kerala.html: Emerald backwaters, misty tea hills, ancient temples, and the gentlest rhythms on Earth.
From the emerald backwaters of Alleppey to the mist-wrapped tea gardens of Munnar, Kerala is a land of extraordinary, quiet beauty. Every shade of green you can imagine.
Houseboat dreams on mirrored lagoons. Kathakali dancers with painted faces. Spice traders in Fort Kochi. Kerala is not just a destination — it's a feeling.
Kerala has 3 international airports: Thiruvananthapuram, Kochi (Cochin), and Calicut. Indian Railways covers the coast beautifully. The scenic train from Shoranur to Nilambur is unmissable.
Grand vegetarian feast on banana leaf — 26 dishes served for Onam.
Pearl spot fish marinated in spices and roasted in banana leaf.
Lacey rice pancakes with aromatic coconut milk vegetable stew.
Heritage-house hostel in Fort Kochi — art, culture, community.
Overnight houseboat on the backwaters — a bucket-list experience.
"An overnight houseboat on the backwaters alone with the stars. I have never felt so at peace in my life."
"Munnar at dawn with mist over the tea gardens is the most beautiful thing I have ever witnessed."
Leeches in forests — tuck trousers in socks
Life jackets on all boat rides
udaipur.html: Palaces that float on lakes, history carved in marble, and sunsets that paint the city gold.
Built around shimmering lakes and crowned by the Aravalli Hills, Udaipur is the most romantic city in India. The City Palace — a 400-year-old architectural marvel — commands Lake Pichola like a king.
Wander narrow bazaars selling miniature paintings, take a shikara across Jag Mandir, watch traditional Rajasthani folk performers under a full moon. Udaipur is pure theatre.

Maharana Pratap Airport (UDR) connects to Delhi, Mumbai, and Jaipur. Well served by trains from Delhi (Chetak Express) and Mumbai (Mewar Express). Udaipur city is best explored by auto-rickshaw or cycle.
Rajasthani royal dish — baked wheat balls with spiced lentils and sweet crumble.
Fiery red mutton curry made with dried Mathania chilies — legendary.
Sweet deep-fried pastry filled with khoya and dry fruits — Jodhpur's gift to Rajasthan.
Heritage-style hostel with lake views and rooftop hangout.
Charming budget stay near City Palace in the old city heart.
"Rented a cycle and went around all 5 lakes at sunrise. The reflection of City Palace in Pichola is unreal."
"The Bagore Ki Haveli folk show at night, sipping chai on a rooftop. Udaipur is a dream."
Fixed price autos exist — negotiate before boarding
Carry sunscreen and water at all times
Wear light cotton in warm months
sikkim.html: Kanchenjunga watches over glacial lakes, ancient monasteries, and valleys of impossible flowers.
India's smallest state hides some of its most staggering landscapes. Gurudongmar Lake — one of the world's highest — reflects a sky so blue it seems painted. Kanchenjunga looms like a guardian god.
Ancient Rumtek and Pemayangtse monasteries echo with butter-lamp prayers. The Yumthang Valley explodes with rhododendrons every spring. Sikkim is sacred India at its most pure.
Fly into Bagdogra Airport (IXB), then take a shared jeep or taxi to Gangtok (4 hrs). Pakyong Airport near Gangtok also has limited connectivity. Inner Line Permits required for North Sikkim.
Strips of dried pork cooked with dry red chilies and radish — Sikkim's signature.
Fermented leafy greens soup — tangy, nourishing, unique to the northeast.
Traditional ring-shaped sweet fried bread made during Tihar and Dashain.
Budget hostel in Gangtok with mountain views and friendly dorm vibes.
Simple, clean, central budget stay in Gangtok — solo-traveller approved.
"Gurudongmar at sunrise with no one else around — I cried. Most spiritual moment of my life."
"Yumthang in rhododendron season is another planet. Sikkim is criminally underrated."
ILP required for North Sikkim, Nathula, Gurudongmar
Arrange permits through Gangtok travel agents
Carry extra passport photos and ID copies
Weather changes rapidly — carry rain gear

kutch.html: A salt desert that stretches to forever, tribal artisans, and the most vivid festival in India.
The Rann of Kutch is a phenomenon. When the salt crust shimmers under a full moon and stretches to a horizon that doesn't exist — you understand why travellers return here again and again.
But Kutch is more than the Rann. The tribal villages of Bhirandiyara, the flamingo-flocked Chhari Dhand, Dholavira's ancient Indus Valley ruins — this is a civilisation unto itself.
Fly into Bhuj Airport from Mumbai or Ahmedabad. Trains from Ahmedabad to Bhuj run regularly (overnight journey). The Rann Utsav season (Nov-Feb) has special camp packages.
Spiced potato filling in a bun with chutneys and pomegranate — India's best street snack.
Comforting Gujarati staple — mung lentil rice with spiced buttermilk curry.
Traditional Gujarati sweet made with wheat flour, ghee, and jaggery.
Government-run luxury tent city at the edge of the Rann — magical.
Budget city hotel — clean, central, solo-traveller friendly.
"Full moon night on the Rann. Just me, the white salt, and the Milky Way. I am still not over it."
"Rann Utsav was incredible — the folk musicians, the camel rides, the embroidery workshops. Pure India."

nagaland.html: Warrior tribes, the Hornbill Festival, and a valley of flowers that blooms in secret.
Nagaland is India's most authentic cultural frontier. Sixteen distinct Naga tribes, each with their own language, costume, and warrior traditions, have preserved their heritage with fierce pride.

The Hornbill Festival in December transforms Kisama Village into the most colourful spectacle in the subcontinent. And then there is Dzukou — a secret valley of seasonal flowers that rewards only those willing to walk for it.
Fly into Dimapur Airport from Kolkata, Delhi, or Guwahati. Then drive to Kohima (3 hrs). Inner Line Permit (ILP) required for all non-residents — get it in Delhi, Kolkata, or at Dimapur.
Fermented soybean with smoky pork — the soul dish of Naga cuisine.
Young bamboo shoots cooked with dried fish and chili — tangy and earthy.
Traditional Naga millet beer — offered at every tribal gathering.
Comfortable budget hotel in the heart of Kohima city.
Stay in a Naga village home — the most authentic travel experience possible.
"Hornbill Festival is like nothing on Earth. 16 tribes, 10 days. I danced with warriors around a fire."
"Dzukou Valley trek was brutal and beautiful. Slept in the valley shelter — woke up in a cloud."
